item.title: Article - Making Sense with MNemo
item.description:
Reference: https://soggywombats.com.au/2024/04/15/making-sense-with-mnemo/

My v1 MNemo with a graphite pencil for note-taking

Like most folks stuck in Melbourne’s lockdown, I didn’t have much to get excited about during 2020. Having finished my cave course in late 2019 and then leaving Mount Gambier under less than ideal circumstances, all I could do was dream about was getting back to explore the caves I was finally qualified to get into. More than just diving and admiring them though, I desperately wanted to get back to try and understand Mount Gambier’s caves - why they’re shaped the way they are, understand how the different rock formations have developed, and (like every new and overly optimistic cave diver) hopefully use all of that to discover something new!

item.title: ChatGPT - Dinaric Karst Belt Expedition
item.description:
Original: https://chatgpt.com/share/6860bcff-0360-8006-8c68-65b3e63a1f15

Best Season to Visit

For a first‐time Balkan cave-diving trip, plan for late August through mid-September. By then the long Adriatic-summer dry spell has lowered groundwater levels, stabilised flow at karst springs and siphons, and delivered the year’s clearest visibility; daytime air still sits in the mid-20 °C range, and water in coastal caves hovers around 18–20 °C. Crucially, most regional clubs schedule their larger expeditions and training camps in this window, making it the easiest period to join fieldwork or gain permit support.(scubadiving.guide, rove.me)

About

The Dinaric Karst Belt (aka Dinaric Alps Karst or Dinarides Karst)

  • One of the most extensive and well-developed karst regions in Europe,
  • Stretches along the western Balkan Peninsula.
  • Primarily associated with the Dinaric Alps,

Spans the following countries:

  • Slovenia
  • Croatia
  • Bosnia & Herzegovina
  • Montenegro
  • Serbia
  • Albania
  • Kosovo

item.title: Notes - Too Many Interests
item.description:
Reference: https://youtu.be/lQFOeC3maeI?si=NVyRDJ759R7_Uhl2

Too Many Interests

You can’t follow your interests if you have no energy

  • Working all day, overstimulation,
  • Unfair to expect all to be able to come home and jump straight in
  • More about energy rather than time
    • How do you enjoy your hobby with a fresh mind and happy outlook
  • Save the heavy stuff for the morning when you’re fresh
    • Probably start to hate the hobby
    • Tired? Focus on relaxed aspects
    • Fresh? Focus on heavy
    • Split hobby elements into “Relaxing” and “Demanding”
  • Look at your energy levels and where you can give best (for me: Mornings)
  • Woodworking vs Camping - Split your hobbies into Relaxing vs Demanding
    • Woodworking you can roll straight into (Relaxing & Rejuvinating)
    • Camping requires more setup & investment (More Demanding)
  • Money
    • Must meet basic needs to fund hobbies
    • Expensive hobbies
    • Money can buy time to embrace hobbies
  • Take a break when you get home
    • Take half an hour to relax and disconnect from work
    • Get back in creative mood
    • Figure out how to have a better break
  • Carve out space for your hobbys/interests
    • Don’t be completely selfless
    • Express that it’s important to you, and an important part of who you are
  • Say no to some of your hobbies (or atleast say no to new ones)
    • The more you do, the more you dilute
    • Kill your darlings
    • Cut it down to 2-3 main hobbies - Intellectual, Physical, Social
  • Hobby Seasons
    • Focus hard on one hobby for several months, then steer away to something else
    • You’ll have muscle memory of the hobby (so you can come back)
    • You’re free to return to any hobby whenever you want
      • If you miss something after you stop, that’s important - you may stick with it your whole life
    • You can’t do everything
  • Busy with other priorities? Find ways to do a little of something you love
    • Let the big thing go, but find small ways to do it instead
    • Reduce the time
  • Quality over Quantity - focused practice
    • Have a plan, set goals, reflect after each session (+ buy quality with coaches)

Common Time Management

item.description:
Use mini keyboard to type before work Productivity

  • Pomodoro, Meditation, speech-to-text, Eat the frog, alarm to go to bed

item.title: Y2038 - Epochalypse
item.description:
On 19 January 2038 at 03:14:07 UTC implementations relying on 32-bit signed integer representations of Unix epoch time will overflow, resulting in a system time of 20:45:52 UTC on 13 December 1901

Time Security SIG - The Time Security SIG exists to help the global FIRST community prepare for the 2036–2038 epoch rollovers. By coordinating research, testing, and outreach on time integrity, the SIG connects CSIRTs, vendors, and standards bodies to strengthen resilience across critical infrastructure. Our goal: ensure the world’s clocks keep running — securely — long past 2038.
